problem: The pump now runs on his manager's say-so
action: Late afternoon on the forecourt. In the mid-ground a manager in a plain shirt is confidently directing things — one arm out, mid-instruction to someone off frame. The dealer stands well apart from him near the edge of the canopy with his hands in his trouser pockets, watching his own forecourt being run by somebody else. He is not part of the action and nobody is looking at him.
lighting: Warm low afternoon sun coming in under the canopy from behind, so the manager is bright in the middle distance and the dealer stands in the cooler shade at the frame edge.
camera: Vertical wide-ish. The dealer is sharp in the foreground right, chest-up but small enough that his separateness reads; the manager is smaller in the middle distance, softer. 35mm.
detail: The manager wears a plain shirt with NO uniform, NO badge, NO logo, NO name tag. No signage anywhere. We do not see the manager's face clearly. Same cream full-sleeve shirt with the sleeves rolled, same dark navy trousers, same watch.
feeling: Being a spectator at your own business. The quiet humiliation of it.
motion: The manager's arm lowers. The dealer does not move at all. A very slow push in on the dealer. No cuts, no camera shake, nobody speaks, no faces turn to camera.

voice_over.hi: अब लगता है पंप मेरा नहीं, मैनेजर का है। जो वो कहे, वही चलता है।
